text_fidelity_a:
Sunlite Cloud-9 Bicycle Suspension Cruiser Saddle, Cruiser Gel, Tri-color Black If you have the type of seat post where the saddle rails are sandwiched/clamped between two contoured plates this saddle might not work on your seat post clamp. This saddle comes with one of those rotary, rotating, claw-type clamps and the saddle likely works fine with that included clamp. However better bike seat posts can't use the included claw clamp type -- they must use their own sandwich-type. Technically, this saddle still should still mount but the distance between the rails was too wide. If you are confused about the difference do a web search for 'bike seat rail clamp' and you'll see the two different families of clamps.

I would have thought that the measured distance between saddle rails would be standardized but the rails on this saddle were just a very few millimeters too wide for both my sandwich-type clamps (it failed to mount on the two different seat post clamps I tried it on). The distance could maybe be lessened by clamping the rails, in a vice, for example, or using some other tool but I decided to return it rather than mess with it..

Otherwise it seemed okay, maybe quite a bit on the stiff side for a gel saddle.
text_fidelity_b: Sunlite Cloud-9 Bicycle Suspension Cruiser Saddle, Cruiser Gel, Tri-color Black

text_fidelity_a:
Livestrong LS8.0E Elliptical Edited 2015

Since the first little hiccups, I haven't had a single problem. Tip - get a professional assemble - it will be worth it. I use it every day and love it - it is the best out there, especially in the price range !

The Pros: The design of the footbeds and stride is ergonomic and I have no joint pain when using it. The levels have sufficient range for absolute beginners to pretty fit people to get a good, safe workout. When working it was very quiet (must have a gym mat).'' Having an elliptical at home is the best.

The cons: There are constantly major things wrong with it (3 service calls in 5 months) and I had it professionally delivered and installed. I am 110 lbs and the only person who uses it. It has now been out of use 10% of the time I have had it. The bolts/bearings on the pivot arm were broken, the flywheel belt and now the flywheel itself. Customer service is disorganized and slow to respond. They have many subcontractors all over who do the fixing and the level of compentency is very variable (2 out of 3 very poor). I would never buy this again nor would I recommend it. Check out reviews from Dicks Sporting goods and other sites. The longevity of this machine is not good and the quality is variable - poor. 800$ is a lot of money to spend on 200lbs of something that I can't use.

Helpful Info about ellipticals in general: You should be aware that ellipticals weigh ~ 200 lbs. You should not only measure length and width at the base to see if it fits in your space, but the height (low ceiling basements will not work with a tall person). Also the area around the machine - how much room you want to the walls. I have a small space, but I wanted to be able to use weights to do upper body, so you need more arm spread .
text_fidelity_b: Livestrong LS8.0E Elliptical

text_fidelity_a:
Bearwill Golf Net, 10x7ft Heavy Duty Golf Practice Net with Golf Mat, Target Cloth, 8 Golf Tees, 6 Golf Balls, Carry Bag, Golf Training Net for Backyard Driving Chipping Indoor Outdoor Training It didn't take me long to figure out how to assemble it, even if there were no instructions. The description says this is heavy duty, and that's why I got it. Not the best golfer in the world, I wanted something that would withstand the chaos and natural disaster that constitutes my golf swing.

It comes with several soft golf balls to hit into the net. This is fine and dandy, but nothing quite replaces the feel of hitting a real, live (so to speak) golf ball. So, I broke out the real buggers and begin hitting into the net. So far, I've hit probably a thousand balls into the net. It's held up well. I leave it assembled and outside, and it's held up to the weather decently. A stiff wind WILL knock it over, however.

As to heavy duty, that's why I only gave it 4 stars. I've hit several of my typical errant shots right off the back bar brace that runs along the back of the net. It's but a nice little dent--a reminder of my burgeoning skills--complete with the golf ball dimples. Currently, I have two such dents. It seems to be holding up despite the abuse, but I expected something called "heavy duty" to withstand such impacts with a yawn and a sheepish grin. No such luck.

One of my spectacularly mishits (again using a real golf ball) hit the back bar with enough force and with the right angle that it deflected over my head and landed on the roof of my house. Hmmm. I was the one with the sheepish grin, yes sir.

I do put two bricks on the sides to keep the net firmly anchored. It does come with its own anchors, but I wasn't able to use them because the ground upon which it sits is too rocky. Not the golf net's problem. That one is my Arizona yard's personal demon. You might not have such a problem.

The hitting mat is awkward in my opinion, being so small, and unless it is anchored it will certainly move when you strike the ball, which is irritating. I even tried to anchor it, but my trench digging golf swings soon uprooted it, much to my annoyance. Also, it will raise the ball up slightly unnaturally, so you will need to find something else to stand on to make sure it is the same height as the mat. Nope, not for me. I bought a 4x5 mat that I could stand on.

Over all, I recommend this net!
text_fidelity_b: Bearwill Golf Net, 10x7ft Heavy Duty Golf Practice Net with Golf Mat, Target Cloth, 8 Golf Tees, 6 Golf Balls, Carry Bag, Golf Training Net for Backyard Driving Chipping Indoor Outdoor Training

When I'm taking the bag with me on a plane I don't want to fully lose one of my carry-on bags to camera equipment. Further, given that this will be the bag I'm storing underneath the seat in front of me, it needs to have space to hold whatever I might want easy access to during the flight, such as a water bottle, food, books, iPad, magazines, jacket, phone charger, etc. Most of the backpack camera bags I looked at had suprsingly little room for non-camera equipment (except for a laptop).

The attached video gives a good idea of how much the bag can hold -- I've loaded it up and then unpacked it.

Pros:

-Tough, rugged construction. No doubt that it can take a beating and protect my camera.
-Even with a large body camera it should be able to hold three lenses (not including the lends attached to the camera).
-Holds laptop and has a good amount of space for non-camera equipment.
-Comes with rain cover; can hold tripod.

Cons:

-Most of the accessory pockets are ridiculously small. For example, the pocket meant for cell phones can barely fit an iPhone 5.

Overall I think this is an excellent bag, but the MSRP price is pretty steep. If it wasn't for the fact that I was able to get the bag for 40% off the MSRP thanks to a one day sale, I would have purchased one of Timbuk2's cheaper camera bags, such as the [[ASIN:B00AMXVKLI Sleuth]] or [[ASIN:B004VD7QU4 Snoop]]. Despite the high price, I'm still going to give the Espionage five starts because it is such a well made camera bag.
text_fidelity_b: Timbuk2 Espionage Camera Backpack, Black, Medium

This cooler is incredibly well-made and I'm thrilled that I got it! (I ended up buying everyone their favorite team's cooler in this same brand, and they were a huge hit over the holidays!)

The first great surprise when it arrived was that it is made by Coleman, with tags on it to prove it. Coleman doesn't make bad stuff, in fact, they have a long history of well-made products, so that was a really nice bonus.

On top of that, there are all kinds of quality extras built into it. For example, when you lift the lid, there is a mesh ice-pack holder built right into the top of it. Then in the front there is a nice zippered compartment that you can securely stash a few things in. The zippers are high quality and the materials, inside and out, are high quality as well. The strap is wide, strong and adjustable. Another nice perk is that it has a little pad where the strap will go over the shoulder, which really makes carrying it much more comfortable. The cooler holds a lot, and really does a great job at keeping things nice and cold. I just put my ice packs in it with our bottles, sandwiches, etc., and we are good to go.

I also got one of these coolers for a friend who is disabled and likes to keep a cooler next to her bed. Well, she'd gotten fed up with coolers that didn't keep things cold for very long and she had switched to using a spaghetti pot (for real!) with ice packs in it, to keep her ginger ale chilled, for constant nausea. She said that with a few frozen ice packs in it, she actually can go two whole days without having to replace the ice packs. She also said it fits great on her scooter when she's on the go.

Made by Coleman, like I said, and with lots of nice features, this high quality cooler is a must-have and a great gift. Check out the same cooler with other team logos. They were offering free gifts for reviews but asked that Amazon reviewers not contact them though Amazon for their “account security”. Probably because this violates Amazon’s rules. I did like it for about a day. Then the blue light died on day two. Still gave it a chance because I can jump rope inside! Counted myself then checked the counter. Perfect match. Tried it again, perfect match. Next two or three times I tried, it didn’t change at all after a good minute or so of jumping. So I tried it off and on for several days. Mixed results. Sometimes it counted perfectly. Sometimes it literally did not count even one jump. Sometimes it did count but was way off. Sometimes it counted Many jumps when I was just holding it in place. It is simply not consistent enough to trust it. If you don’t care about the electronic counter, it is just okay.

text_fidelity_a:
SKLZ Pure Path Golf Swing Trainer Yellow, Large For anyone just learning the game of golf, like me, this SKLZ Pure Path Swing Trainer With Instant Feedback is wonderful. We have clay soil here in Ohio and it went into the ground really solid with a bit of pushing, then stepping down on it. I used my Taylor Made Burner Driver and all my irons every day for a week hitting the plastic ball and this trainer's spikes only had to be stepped down just a little bit once. It really doesn't move at all when it's pushed down in solid clay soil.

Being a new golfer, I have been learning to just hit the ball, focusing on my grip and how to swing. My husband takes me to putting greens and driving ranges- but when you just want to learn to make contact with the ball- it is quite expensive paying for those buckets at the driving ranges. I love this Swing Trainer, as it costs me nothing. You can set it up as you like, with three different ball heights, and being able to connect with the ball with your club coming up right under it, is just like the driving range.

The best part is, I don't have to chase after any plastic balls in the yard, I don't have to pay for buckets of balls, and that leaves me just time for concentrating on making contact with the ball. Not only that, but when you hit the ball, you can watch the yellow rope spin straight, to the right or to the left. I can actually see in which direction I'm hitting it. I know once I get my swing better, make good contact with the ball, feel my grip getting comfortable, and see most of my shots going straight, I'll be back on the driving range. But until then, I can practice making ball contact and see if I'm shooting the ball straight- right in my own back yard and the cost is nothing, which is just perfect for me.
text_fidelity_b: SKLZ Pure Path Golf Swing Trainer Yellow, Large

My wife has been using such tiny charing ports for years (like us all) and she’s very careful. This thing easily popped off and in spite of her dainty skills at repairing such tiny things, cannot get it back on. That’s a minus for us.

But as a tool, it’s great. So if they can fix that flaw in how the port cover is attached, we’d be happy to give it a 5.

It arrived in a nice box (for yourself or a gift) in 3 parts: light, clamp, and charger. She charged right away - after as she pushed the piece in it popped off - and we put it on. She severely broke her foot a couple weeks ago and gets around for the next 3 months on a scooter. But she wants to be able to see at night if she’s moving through the house, or if we are outside, so we thought a bike light might work. It’s perfect for that. It fits on the handles of her scooter as easily as a bike - and we plan on switching it to a bike when she’s recovered. In the mean time, the 3 levels of light mean she can see safely in the house without being disruptive, and she can see safely outside moving to the car or around our home. It’s really easy to clamp and remove - she takes it off when we are in the car so it won’t get broken off. And she can easily pop it back on.

Overall this is a great light and minus the flaw with the port cover, we are really happy with it. That we cannot overlook, however, because there is little doubt that in 12+ weeks on the scooter and future use on the bike, covering the port hole would be a safety issue (rain). So the 4 star has to stay. Happy to have it though.

Here's why not: I received the club on Wednesday, put it in my bag and went to the course on Thursday. Looks like a Taylormade Rescue, but with really poor detail. Well, looks don't get the ball down the course, and it was $20, so who cares, right?

First shot, nicely impressed...second shot, the same. Third shot, I feel something...odd. Ball pops straight up in the air at almost a 90 degree angle to my lie. Look at the club, and there's the answer. Clubhead is an inch down the shaft from the ferrule, and with the slightest tug, it pops right off. So much for the experiment.

Maybe I'm crazy, but there's just no excuse for a clubhead falling off within three shots; six swings total with practice. None. Zero. I'm surprised it actually made it through shipping without coming off. Maybe they used cornstarch to glue this on instead of epoxy? Who knows. The only saving grace is that I hadn't yet thrown away the box, so it was easy to return this dismal thing.

yellow = extra light = 2-4 lbs resistance
blue = light = 4-6 lbs resistance
green = medium = 10-12 lbs resistance
black = heavy = 15-20 lbs resistance
red = extra heavy = 25-30 lbs resistance

You choose a band with the desired resistance, clip it to the 2 handles or a handle and the Velcro ankle strap, and do the desired exercises. There's also a "door anchor" nylon strap with a fat weight in one end. You thread the exercise band through the loop on one end on the anchor, then place it along the edge of the door and close the door. The fat end prevents the strap from slipping through the gape in the door and thus you can do some exercises with the exercise band centered above or level with you. This does, however, put some stress on the door. Not so much with the lighter weights, but I suspect it would with the heavier weights. The equipment seems well-made and so far I've had no problems with it in its first week of light use. They have a book with 18 exercises described and several illustrated with a color photo. They provide a lifetime warranty.

Some of their warnings:
-Do not overstretch the resistance bands [though they don't say exactly how far is too far]
-Always wear safety glasses when using resistance bands [and safety glasses are not included]

Rule number two of lightweight bicycle components is everything must be installed with a torque wrench. If you read stories of Thomson components failing soon after purchase, the bolts have been torqued too much.

Seatpost looks sleek, though the setback version is an acquired taste. The adjustability is excellent and the side markers allow you to set your seat angle with a great deal of precision. I'll probably buy another one.

Super Paddles Stand Up Paddle - 3-Piece Adjustable SUP Paddle Alloy Series Sport - Aluminum Shaft, Nylon Blade This paddle has been great for our stand up paddle board! This is the second one purchased so I will be comparing it to a $35 paddle that was bought from a big box sporting goods store that starts with the letter A. We will call this Paddle A for comparison.

Out of the box, the Super Paddle seemed to be fairly comparable to Paddle A. Both were lightweight and could be disassembled for storage. The Super Paddle had some distinct advantages that quickly became evident as it was used:

• Packs Smaller: The Super Paddle pieces are better designed to break down into an easily portable size. The thought put into this feature was appreciated.

• Wider Blade: The Super Paddle had a wider blade than Paddle A, giving you more forward momentum with each stroke and more powerful maneuverability overall. It was noted that the Super Paddle blade was standing up to wear, tear and scratches much better than Paddle A.

• Sturdier: When it was assembled, the Super Paddle shaft felt very sturdy and firm in your hand. Paddle A was acceptable in this regard but it was noted that the Super Paddle was the one that seemed to be preferred, no matter who was on the board.

The Super Paddle was used by several family members on an 11 foot Alpine Explorer Stand Up Paddle Board (SUP). Everyone ages 55 to 9 was able to use the paddle board and the Super Paddle easily on the open water. The paddle is adjustable for persons 5 feet and above but even our 4’8” (56 inch) tall paddlers were easily able to use the Super Paddle for learning to SUP and exploring around the lake. If it is dropped by an inexperienced beginner, it is no big deal since the paddle floats.

I was fortunate to be able to purchase this piece of sporting equipment at a significant discount to try it out with family members on the SUP (and snap some pictures!) before writing this review and comparing the two paddles. We hope our review and the pictures of our fun help you to make the best buying decision for your family!
text_fidelity_b: Super Paddles Stand Up Paddle - 3-Piece Adjustable SUP Paddle Alloy Series Sport - Aluminum Shaft, Nylon Blade

Fitbit Flex 2, Navy (US Version) This is my second Fitbit but my first Fitbit Flex (I have used the One in the past). I really like it and haven't had any problems with the accuracy.

I love the community involved when you use the Fitbit brand (challenges with friends and family to keep you going). I REALLY like that this is water proof- I haven't gone swimming with it on yet, but it's nice that I don't have to think about it when I shower or when I'm washing the dishes.

It is a relatively small and simple design. There are 5 lights on the top, 4 to indicate the proportion of your daily steps you've done that day (with the goal of 10,000) and the fifth to give you notices. You have to remember what each of the colors is, but I haven't had any problems with that- green to indicate when you're checking on your steps, red to tell you your battery is getting low, and blue or purple when you're getting a phone call or text (I'm not totally sure about these as I don't use them for that). You can connect to you phone to notify you when you get a phone call or text message; you get get hourly reminders to move; you can track your sleep schedule; and what I love the most about is that you can seamlessly change activity type (running, elliptical, swimming, outdoor biking) without manipulating the information on your app.

Easy and comfortable. I have definitely found that it has helped me increase my daily steps!
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Flex 2, Navy (US Version)

text_fidelity_a:
Sit N Cycle sitNcycle SNC2 Dorothy Hamill Deluxe XL Low Resistance Exercise Bike This is a low resistance exercise bike. The design is surprisingly solid, with one major problem: the belts are the wrong size!

This is why most people have torn belts in these things. Belt replacement is a major repair, requiring box/socket wrenches and allens, belt routing and careful tension adjustment and alignment.

The good news is that I figured out what belts do work in this thing:
4PJ610 (the wide belt, this is the same as OEM)
3PJ610 (the narrow belt, this is longer than OEM which was 3PJ584).
You can buy belts from Ametric, that's the only place I found.

You could probably get a shorter wide belt instead, but the combination above works pretty well - if tightened sufficiently, there is quite a bit of resistance in this bike.

The reason you want a longer narrow belt is because the tension adjustment is done on both belts at the same time, and the narrow belt is then overtightened and soon rips. Hope this helps you.

I also discarded all the plastic body parts, it's a naked bike now. After taking this thing apart twice, you'll want to do the same...

I sit on this bike when I work at my height-adjustable desk, sometimes all day.
text_fidelity_b: Sit N Cycle sitNcycle SNC2 Dorothy Hamill Deluxe XL Low Resistance Exercise Bike

So when I got these balls it was for at home, on the putting green, and our occasional foray onto the course. Honestly, these are fun - there is NO way I'm taking them to a driving range - wouldn't want to loose them!

We set up the putting green and got to it. We'll use them one at a time (for longevity) and so far love them. It's been fun playing in the house. My wife recently severely broke her foot, so she's limited - I figured she could get some exercise safely, and we have had a few really fun hours playing. You'll thrown them against the ground to activate, then play like normal. I mentioned our lack of time on the course because I cannot legitimately compare them to what a normal ball would feel like, but for us they feel on point - like anything we've hit. The glow is great. Lights on or off we've had fun. As you can see, it's easy to see either way. And they are very attractive to cats... who only add to the obstacles for a little indoor miniature golf challenge. Note on this fur - you can see how much they throw that light.

Overall these are just really fun. I'm sure it would be cool hitting one for distance (again, don't want to loose it - as if you could). We were playing and suddenly it went off - had only been putting, so no hard hit, which may keep it on longer. I'd say it was within 5 minutes it went off. But this is a fun way to enjoy the game and we're glad to have them. I would most surely get another set.

text_fidelity_a:
Keiser M3i Indoor Cycle Bundle I've had this bike a few months now. It is quiet (but not silent, there is a noise from the drive belt) but it is very smooth and responsive.

Assembly was straight-forward, but unless you want to find all the tools you need to assemble it yourself, I would recommend getting the tool package available on their website. The torque wrench was our deciding factor in just buying their kit. Keiser offers a discount on the tool package if you purchase it with the bike directly on their website.

Things to know: the app is TERRIBLE. Other reviewers have already listed all the bugs in depth, but the app is unreliable for recording workouts and is not user-friendly. The bike also will not work directly with other apps (like Peloton). For that you need the converter, which costs another $200 on top of this bike, unless you buy the bike directly from their website. Then it is only $50. Considering they were discounting it 75% with purchase of the bike, I consider $200 a rip-off for what your bike should have done in the first place (work with other apps). I wrote customer service about the bugs. They agreed there was a problem and the developer would be notified. I was told I would be updated when it was fixed. I never was. The problem in the app still persists as of my writing this review.

Customer service: I wrote customer service via email. As far as timeliness, they wrote back quickly. However, if I ever had more than one question in my message, one, and only one, of my questions would be answered. I had to write back multiple times for my additional questions to be answered, so one simple email took several days to be fully addressed. As stated above, some of the issues never were.

I will update the review if any issues with the bike itself come up. I love the bike, how smooth it runs, and the huge range of resistances available. It seems well-designed and like it will hold up. However, there are some big annoyances that will cost you extra $$$ to overcome.
text_fidelity_b: Keiser M3i Indoor Cycle Bundle

The other rod was rigged with a fluke swim Jr and I could easily cast it to docks and structure. I fished a whole Saturday with only those 2 combos. I picked up the phantom x on the piscifun rod, man it felt heavy compared to the other 2. But it is a medium/heavy rod compared to the falcons medium. I've got 7 bait casting rods on the boat now, but I'll mainly be fishing these Ms with the falcon rods. I might in the future step up to the top tier reel, but these Ms throw the lure further than I've ever been able to with other equipment. Great little reels, just lube them up before going out with them.

(Update)
Both of these reels became very stiff to release to cast at the beginning of this year. One doesn't trip the release upon trying to crank back in. So I guess they are good for one to two seasons

text_fidelity_a: Chief Tac Military Tactical Molle Vest Mesh Light Army Airsoft Paintball Utility Vest, Breathable Lightweight Hunting Fishing Vest for Men Women For less than $50, and you can find them occasionally on sale/discount, this was almost exactly what I wanted.  I wanted a vest I could wear OVER my armor carrier, and this fit the bill.  I know it says "paintball" in the title/description.  As a former paintball player and paintball field owner and Blackhawk gear dealer, I can tell you so far this vest is very good.  If I am not satisfied later, I will come back and modify my rating.  The first thing I checked out was the zipper.  The zipper seems to be very strong and very good.  Also, there are 2 small speed fastener buckles across the chest.  Normally, I don't like anything adding more bulk, but these fasteners SHOULD help keep that zipper from pulling apart.  I have put attachments on and off and back on and off this vest, and the vest has done very well so far.  The vest is highly adjustable and customizable.  Again, this fit my special purpose of having a body armor carrier underneath with the vest with all my gear on top of the armor carrier.  I wanted to be able to still wear my armor even after I took my tactical vest off, and this fit the bill almost perfectly.  MOLLE attachment points all over this thing makes it possible to set up pretty much however someone wants, and it's still not too bulky for me.  5 stars for now.
text_fidelity_b: Chief Tac Military Tactical Molle Vest Mesh Light Army Airsoft Paintball Utility Vest, Breathable Lightweight Hunting Fishing Vest for Men Women

Bright Bike Light, 1000 Lumens Bicycle Front and Back Bicycle Light Set, Large Capacity Battery Rechargeable Road Bike Lights, Waterproof Bike Lights Set We needed a light for evening commuting on our folding bikes. This fit the bill.

The front light does a VERY good job of keeping the city streets in view. It is 3x as bright as the typical tiny lights people add to their city commuting bikes and it can be seen from blocks away. You can be sure cars headed towards you will be aware of your presence.

The rear light has a large number of flash patterns and brightness settings. Its also a decent size, so you can be sure you're visible from the rear.

The fastening system for the front light is very secure, but you'll likely need to cut some excess plastic after you've set it up or you'll have a single long strand pointing at you from your handlebars... The rear light uses the typical rubber connectors which work fine on seat posts or on the backs of some types of cycling helmets. The kit includes extra fastening material for the front and rear lights - which is a GREAT addition.

Battery life seems appropriate. We've used it for three evenings of 30 minute commuting and have not had to recharge yet.

Recommended.

text_fidelity_a:
Graphite Pickleball Paddles Set of 4, 2023 USAPA Approved, Carbon Fiber Surface (CHS), Polypropylene Lightweight Honeycomb Core, 3 Indoor 3 Outdoor Pickleball, 4 Replacement Soft Grip + Bag I like that this comes with its own little zippered carrying case. That's just an extra that makes it nicer than having to find a duffel-bag or some other place to carry the set.

It comes with 4 paddles that are the same except for the colors. It has 3 indoor and 3 outdoor balls which are almost identical except for the spacing of the holes. They're like Whiffle™ balls. The holes prevent them from going too far from the air resistance. The ones for indoors are the ones with the bigger holes because you can't hit them as far.

I know it says that you can play indoors and technically that's true, but it depends on where you're playing. A big game room with lots of space would work. A place where you can trip over furniture or knock over lamps isn't a good idea. It also depends on how aggressive you want to be with your swings. The indoor balls are not the problem because they couldn't easily build up enough momentum to break anything except very delicate or top-heavy things. But the paddles swinging around are more of the issue with playing indoors. A big swing or stretch if you aren't aware of the stuff around you could be where you'd break something or trip over something. But still, about the same level of caution you'd have with Ping-Pong, but without the table to keep you in place.

The paddles are pretty nice quality and lighter than they look like they should be. But they have a lot of surface area and the balls are easier to hit than with Ping-Pong paddles.

You'll have to look up the rules online because they aren't included, but really that's only if you want to play "official Pickle-ball". You can play it with Ping-pong rules, badminton rules, volleyball rules, tennis rules -- just about any of the similar kind of games that I can think of -- it's just a bit easier and has requires less skill or movement. It's really about the same level of activity that you'd have with badminton and the same sized area if you're playing outdoors.

Personally, indoors is just if we want to play "hit-the-ball-back-and-forth-down-the-hallway" because it's too hot/cold/wet outside.

This doesn't come with a net, and I thought the rubberband strips might have been to map out the court area, but it's supposed to be for the grip on the paddles. If you're going to play "official" you'll need a net which is pretty much the same as a badminton net just not as high. It's basically a mini tennis court with much the same net.

It's good exercise, and I can't imagine this being a competitive sport, but I was wrong about tag being an 'official' sport when I heard someone mention it -- but it actually is and surprisingly fun to watch -- with sponsors and everything. Pickleball might be the same because why wouldn't someone take something that's fun and add a bunch of rules so they can make some money from advertising.

It's good for staying active and just about everyone likes to play because we don't play with any real rules. Not because we have odd ideas like "there are no losers here", but because it's just that unimportant.

I can't comment on the price with the way things are these days, but it seems to be about the same price as other options, and the quality is decent. The bag is a bonus and even the dog likes to play -- but that's where it goes from being 'pickle-ball' to 'slobber-ball'.

Overall, this is a nice set, especially the paddles. Five stars.
text_fidelity_b: Graphite Pickleball Paddles Set of 4, 2023 USAPA Approved, Carbon Fiber Surface (CHS), Polypropylene Lightweight Honeycomb Core, 3 Indoor 3 Outdoor Pickleball, 4 Replacement Soft Grip + Bag

text_fidelity_a: Coleman Camping Tent with Instant Setup, 4/6/8/10 Person Weatherproof Tent with Integrated Rainfly, Double-Thick Fabric, and Included Carry Bag, Sets Up in 60 Seconds I am slow brained at mechanical things and my first Coleman tent I bought a decade ago took way too much time and frustration from my vacation in the great outdoors to figure out and it had too many pieces so I had to keep referencing the manual.  Plus I had to buy a duffle bag to keep it in because no average human could refit it in the case it came in.  Looks like Coleman too was slow brained, but now it's the opposite with this tent.  It really did take just a few minutes my first time setting it up.  I'm sure my second will be 60 seconds or less.  And afterward I was able to fit it in the carrying case, though I wish it were just a little bigger because I needed help squishing the sides together when zipping...like me now at size 14 trying to get into my wedding dress of 30 years ago.  I'm so glad I can put the tent up by myself.  I use an extra long cot from Walmart and had to set it on the diagonal to fit and even then it's poking the tent fabric a little on the outside.  There isn't much room left on either side of the cot's interior.  I'll keep this tent, but I wish I bought the tent for six people, even though I often camp alone.  I like having space to set a little desk and walk around.  I haven't been in rain yet, but I did spray the outside with water repellant.  I looked all around at the seams and didn't see the seam irregularities some here complained about.  It looks really pro.  In the middle of the day I went inside to take a nap on a day that was about 80-85 degrees.  It was pretty warm even with all the windows unzipped.  The sun was beating down directly overhead, so I'm ordering the rain top even though it doesn't rain much in So CA.  I'm thinking and hoping that maybe that rain top will deflect some of the heat from direct sunlight.  If you too are slow brained, I'd strongly suggest watching some online videos like on YouTube to see how people set up this tent before you begin.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Camping Tent with Instant Setup, 4/6/8/10 Person Weatherproof Tent with Integrated Rainfly, Double-Thick Fabric, and Included Carry Bag, Sets Up in 60 Seconds
